definition: The offline half of RAG: parsing source documents (PDF, HTML, DOCX, scans), cleaning, chunking, enriching with metadata, embedding, and indexing.
details: The offline half of RAG: parsing source documents (PDF, HTML, DOCX, scans), cleaning, chunking, enriching with metadata, embedding, and indexing. Most real-world RAG failures trace back to ingestion (bad parsing, broken tables, lost structure) rather than the model.

explainer.lead: The offline half of retrieval-augmented generation that turns raw source documents into an indexed, searchable store. It matters because most real-world RAG failures trace back to ingestion, not the model.

tiers.eli5: Like preparing ingredients before cooking: washing, chopping and labelling them so the meal later goes smoothly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers parse PDF, HTML, DOCX and scans, clean and chunk the text, enrich it with metadata, embed it and index it. The pitfall is bad parsing, broken tables and lost structure, which silently degrade retrieval.
tiers.paperLevel: The offline stage of RAG comprising parsing, cleaning, chunking, metadata enrichment, embedding and indexing; no formal bound exists, but failures concentrate in parsing and structure loss.

explainer.example: A scanned PDF with broken tables is parsed, cleaned, split into chunks with metadata, embedded, and indexed for later retrieval.
